children: Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures rebounded on Tuesday after hitting a four-week low the previous day, with traders' attention turning to coming US stocks data and a rain-soaked harvest in parts of the Midwest.

Traders had been focused on last week's US-China summit, which underwhelmed the market and drove down prices on Monday. The steep decline encouraged buyers to emerge before the US Department of Agriculture issues a quarterly stocks report on Wednesday, traders said. They also adjusted positions before the end of the month and quarter.
"Part of it is we just dropped too much yesterday," said Don Roose, president of brokerage US Commodities. "We're still wet in the western corn belt, and basis levels are still strong."
The most active CBOT soybeans contract
was up 12-3/4 cents at $13.01 a bushel after dropping on Monday to the lowest since August 31 at $12.79-1/4.
The benchmark set its highest in nearly three years this month in the run-up to last week's meeting between US President

and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping. The absence of additional Chinese purchase commitments for US soybeans and soybeans' absence from a list of US agricultural goods set for tariff cuts disappointed traders.
They were monitoring US harvesting this week after forecasters said rain will continue to slow progress over the next week.

US farmers had harvested 17% of the soybean crop and 18% of the corn crop as of Sunday, the USDA said on Monday. That matched the average pace over the past five years but was below average analyst expectations of 20% for both crops. States including
Basis levels, or the difference between futures and cash prices, remained solid after rain delayed harvesting in the western Midwest, traders said.
USDA's report on Wednesday is expected to show corn stocks were 1.918 billion bushels at September 1, up from 1.551 billion a year earlier, a Reuters poll of analysts showed.

rose 3-1/2 cents to $6.92-1/4 a bushel after falling to its lowest since August 19.
